# Utility device

This is the canonical partial contract for `SURF-DEVICE-UTILITY` under
FEAT-DEVICES / FEAT-AUDIO in the [feature map](feature-map.md), following
[ADR 0005](../decisions/adr-0005-full-live-specification-coverage.md).
Inputs, controls, observable outputs and state are specified below; numerical
algorithms and unsupported lifecycle outcomes remain explicit gaps.

**D12 exact-target U:** D12 means the captured current official Version 12 manual,
not an observation of Live 12.4.3. Every D12 clause's exact-build applicability
is U. Dpkg means direct observation of retained files shipped in the target
package; it grades only stored bytes/values. No S or X audio/display claim is
made. U has no oracle and must never pass. All application cases are unexecuted.
This page is an analyst draft, not a released implementation input or complete
device specification. [Research and source limits](../research/device-audio-utilities.md)
own evidence synthesis; this page owns behavior.

The [device-chain/rack contract](device-racks.md) owns generic insertion,
reordering, activation, preset actions and deletion. [Set structure](live-set-structure.md)
and [ALS container](als-container.md) own their stated container/structure scopes;
their T1 device subset does not prove Utility save/reopen. [Automation](automation-envelopes.md)
owns its envelope representation/evaluation clauses, not untraced device scheduling.
[Mix graph](mix-graph.md) owns track routing/mixing. [Mixer values](mixer-values.md)
describes track faders; it does not supply this device's gain, pan or smoothing law.
The current-manual source does not settle platform differences, keyboard access,
permissions, recovery, latency or transport coupling beyond explicit clauses.

## Requirements

### REQ-DEVICE-UTILITY-001 — audio input and output

**D12.** Input is the stereo audio arriving at this device-chain position; output is the signal processed by the selected Utility controls. Device insertion, ordering, deletion and generic activation belong to SPEC-DEVICE-RACKS. The manual does not establish a complete processing order among Utility controls.

Evidence: `utility:B02–B14`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-UTILITY-002 — independent phase controls

**D12.** Provide separate Left and Right Phase controls that invert the corresponding input-channel phase. The composition order with channel selection, Mono, Width, Bass Mono, gain and balance is U. This clause does not specify coefficient precision, latency or ramping.

Evidence: `utility:B03`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-UTILITY-003 — channel selection

**D12.** Channel Mode can select the Left source: ignore the right source and present the left source on both outputs. The documented disablement rule also names Right mode. Right-mode sample routing, the full mode list and numeric enum-to-label mapping require separate evidence; preset filenames do not prove those laws.

Evidence: `utility:B04, B07`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-UTILITY-004 — Width

**D12.** Width 0% gives mono; values greater than 100% widen the stereo panorama. If Channel Mode is Left or Right, Width is disabled and has no function. Complete domain, width matrix, normalization, 100% identity and behavior for already mono input are U.

Evidence: `utility:B05, B07`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-UTILITY-005 — Mid/Side view and endpoints

**D12.** The Width context menu switches between Width and Mid/Side controls. At 100M audio is summed to mono; from 0 toward 100S the stereo/out-of-phase components are emphasized. At 100S only the side signal is heard and the output channels are 180 degrees out of phase. Left/Right Channel Mode disables this control. Parameter remapping, endpoint gain and remembered hidden values are U.

Evidence: `utility:B06–B07`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-UTILITY-006 — Mono

**D12.** Enabling Mono converts stereo input to mono. Summing coefficients and interactions with Channel Mode, Width/Mid-Side, Bass Mono, phase and Balance are U.

Evidence: `utility:B08`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-UTILITY-007 — Bass Mono cutoff

**D12.** Enabling Bass Mono converts low frequencies to mono. Bass Mono Frequency adjusts a cutoff over 50–500 Hz. Filter type, order, slope, crossover phase, normalization and exact response around cutoff are U.

Evidence: `utility:B09`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-UTILITY-008 — Bass Mono Audition

**D12.** Enabling Bass Mono Audition makes only the low frequencies audible. Dependence on the Bass Mono switch, cutoff transition and bypass/off behavior are U.

Evidence: `utility:B10`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-UTILITY-009 — Gain domain

**D12.** Gain adjusts the input level over minus infinity dB through +35 dB. No linear-to-dB formula, numerical floor, float precision, automation interpolation, clipping or smoothing is claimed. Track fader laws from SPEC-MIXER-VALUES have not been traced to this device and do not apply by name alone.

Evidence: `utility:B11`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-UTILITY-010 — Gain arrow editing

**D12.** Up/down arrow editing changes Gain in 1 dB steps between −18 and +35 dB; between −18 and minus infinity the adjustment smoothly accelerates. Repetition cadence, exact lower-region sequence, endpoint key handling and text-entry parsing are U.

Evidence: `utility:B11`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-UTILITY-011 — Balance

**D12.** Balance pans the signal within the stereo field. Pan law, center gain, normalized storage range, extreme-channel attenuation, mono behavior and coupling with other controls are U.

Evidence: `utility:B12`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-UTILITY-012 — Mute at chain position

**D12.** Mute silences the incoming signal at Utility’s device-chain position. Utility can precede a delay or reverb and mute its input without switching off that downstream device’s output. Tail waveform/duration is owned by the downstream effect and is not specified here.

Evidence: `utility:B13`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-UTILITY-013 — DC filtering

**D12.** DC filters out DC offsets and extremely low frequencies below the audible range. Cutoff, filter response, startup/transient behavior, numerical precision and interaction order are U. The manual’s audibility discussion does not establish sample-exact output.

Evidence: `utility:B14`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-UTILITY-014 — retained preset state vocabulary

**Dpkg.** The retained StereoGain schema and ten shipped presets establish named stored fields and exact saved values, summarized in the research packet. They do not establish constructor defaults, accepted malformed ranges, load/save normalization or live UI state. LegacyGain and LegacyMode are retained historical fields; their migration semantics are U.

Evidence: `PKG-SCHEMA:StereoGain; package-values.json device=Utility`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-UTILITY-015 — lifecycle and numerical gaps

**U.** Exact 12.4.3 applicability of every D12 clause is U. Save/reopen, preset replace/hot-swap, undo/redo, aborted edits, invalid numeric text, malformed files, automation scheduling, sample-rate/block-size changes, suspension, audio-device failure, deletion and teardown require outcome evidence. This draft provides finite ungraded probes, not invented success behavior.

Evidence: `No outcome evidence`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

# Tuner device

This is the canonical partial contract for `SURF-DEVICE-TUNER` under
FEAT-DEVICES / FEAT-AUDIO in the [feature map](feature-map.md), following
[ADR 0005](../decisions/adr-0005-full-live-specification-coverage.md).
Inputs, controls, observable outputs and state are specified below; numerical
algorithms and unsupported lifecycle outcomes remain explicit gaps.

**D12 exact-target U:** D12 means the captured current official Version 12 manual,
not an observation of Live 12.4.3. Every D12 clause's exact-build applicability
is U. Dpkg means direct observation of retained files shipped in the target
package; it grades only stored bytes/values. No S or X audio/display claim is
made. U has no oracle and must never pass. All application cases are unexecuted.
This page is an analyst draft, not a released implementation input or complete
device specification. [Research and source limits](../research/device-audio-utilities.md)
own evidence synthesis; this page owns behavior.

The [device-chain/rack contract](device-racks.md) owns generic insertion,
reordering, activation, preset actions and deletion. [Set structure](live-set-structure.md)
and [ALS container](als-container.md) own their stated container/structure scopes;
their T1 device subset does not prove Tuner save/reopen. [Automation](automation-envelopes.md)
owns its envelope representation/evaluation clauses, not untraced device scheduling.
[Mix graph](mix-graph.md) owns track routing/mixing. [Mixer values](mixer-values.md)
describes track faders; it does not supply this device's gain, pan or smoothing law.
The current-manual source does not settle platform differences, keyboard access,
permissions, recovery, latency or transport coupling beyond explicit clauses.

## Requirements

### REQ-DEVICE-TUNER-001 — measurement input and transparent output

**D12.** Analyze incoming monophonic pitch and its distance from the nearest semitone. Tuner is a measurement device and does not alter the incoming audio. Clean monophonic signals are the intended input; polyphonic, noisy or harmonically rich inputs may give inaccurate results. No error or polyphonic-detection fallback is promised.

Evidence: `tuner:B02–B03`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-TUNER-002 — view switching and tuning color

**D12.** The lower-left view buttons switch between Classic and Histogram views. Both use green for in tune and red for out of tune. Detection/green thresholds, hysteresis, intermediate colors and hold time are U.

Evidence: `tuner:B05`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-TUNER-003 — Classic display

**D12.** Classic View shows a colored ball along a curve, the nearest detected note name in the center, and side arrows indicating whether tuning must move up or down. Exact note/octave spelling, pixels, ball displacement law and arrow thresholds are U.

Evidence: `tuner:B07`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-TUNER-004 — Target Mode direction

**D12.** Target Mode has a central outline for desired pitch. The signal is in tune when the ball lies exactly within the outline; a sharp signal appears to its right, a flat signal to its left. This describes display semantics, not a quantified accepted cents band.

Evidence: `tuner:B08`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-TUNER-005 — Strobe Mode

**D12.** Strobe Mode replaces the curve with a rotating light band. Rightward rotation means sharp; leftward means flat; a greater detuning makes the band move faster. Rotation speed, reference tolerance and freeze behavior are U.

Evidence: `tuner:B09`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-TUNER-006 — Hertz and cents readout

**D12.** A switch selects incoming absolute frequency in Hz or distance from target in cents, and is visible in both Classic and Histogram views. Exact rounding, displayed precision, cents conversion, note-boundary tie handling and octave labeling are U.

Evidence: `tuner:B10, B14`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-TUNER-007 — Histogram

**D12.** Histogram shows pitch over time and note names on its right scale. Horizontal gray lines indicate in-tune note centers; sharp notes lie above their lines and flat notes below. History length, vertical units, update cadence and handling of missing detections are U.

Evidence: `tuner:B12`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-TUNER-008 — Histogram navigation and Auto

**D12.** Dragging vertically scrolls pitches; dragging horizontally zooms. Auto centers the display on incoming pitch. Auto/manual precedence, zoom limits and view-state retention are U.

Evidence: `tuner:B13`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-TUNER-009 — note spelling menu

**D12.** Right-clicking anywhere within the view exposes three spelling choices: sharps, flats, or sharps and flats. Spelling changes labels; no pitch-processing change is documented. Exact key- or tuning-system-dependent enharmonic selection is U.

Evidence: `tuner:B16–B19`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-TUNER-010 — reference pitch

**D12.** Reference changes the tuning reference used to analyze input; documented default is 440 Hz with an adjustable domain 410–480 Hz. Exact increment, text parsing, runtime default corroboration, reference convention under nonstandard tuning systems and output indication tolerances are U.

Evidence: `tuner:B21`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-TUNER-011 — target persisted fields

**Dpkg.** The retained Tuner schema and Guitar Recording template show tuning frequency, view/readout/strobe state, histogram state, accidental spelling and IgnoreTuningSystem. The historical template stores TuningFreq/Manual=440. This is a saved example, not a 12.4.3 constructor/default or tuning-system behavioral contract.

Evidence: `PKG-SCHEMA:Tuner; package-values.json device=Tuner`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-TUNER-012 — unresolved detection and lifecycle

**U.** Exact 12.4.3 applicability of every D12 clause remains U. Pitch algorithm, supported frequency/level/sample-rate range, confidence, silence/noise/polypitch fallback, latency, channel combination, transients, tuning-system interaction, persistence, automation, undo, cancellation, invalid files and teardown are unknown. No zero-cent or note-accuracy tolerance is invented.

Evidence: `No outcome evidence`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

# Spectrum device

This is the canonical partial contract for `SURF-DEVICE-SPECTRUM` under
FEAT-DEVICES / FEAT-AUDIO in the [feature map](feature-map.md), following
[ADR 0005](../decisions/adr-0005-full-live-specification-coverage.md).
Inputs, controls, observable outputs and state are specified below; numerical
algorithms and unsupported lifecycle outcomes remain explicit gaps.

**D12 exact-target U:** D12 means the captured current official Version 12 manual,
not an observation of Live 12.4.3. Every D12 clause's exact-build applicability
is U. Dpkg means direct observation of retained files shipped in the target
package; it grades only stored bytes/values. No S or X audio/display claim is
made. U has no oracle and must never pass. All application cases are unexecuted.
This page is an analyst draft, not a released implementation input or complete
device specification. [Research and source limits](../research/device-audio-utilities.md)
own evidence synthesis; this page owns behavior.

The [device-chain/rack contract](device-racks.md) owns generic insertion,
reordering, activation, preset actions and deletion. [Set structure](live-set-structure.md)
and [ALS container](als-container.md) own their stated container/structure scopes;
their T1 device subset does not prove Spectrum save/reopen. [Automation](automation-envelopes.md)
owns its envelope representation/evaluation clauses, not untraced device scheduling.
[Mix graph](mix-graph.md) owns track routing/mixing. [Mixer values](mixer-values.md)
describes track faders; it does not supply this device's gain, pan or smoothing law.
The current-manual source does not settle platform differences, keyboard access,
permissions, recovery, latency or transport coupling beyond explicit clauses.

## Requirements

### REQ-DEVICE-SPECTRUM-001 — analysis and transparent audio

**D12.** Spectrum performs real-time analysis of incoming audio; its graph has vertical dB and horizontal frequency/pitch axes. It is a measurement tool and does not alter incoming audio. Graph refresh timing and audio-through precision/latency are U.

Evidence: `spectrum:B02`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-SPECTRUM-002 — Block measurement size

**D12.** Block chooses the number of samples analyzed per measurement. Larger settings improve accuracy and increase CPU demand according to the manual. The supported sample-count list, FFT size mapping, overlap, zero padding and accuracy/CPU bounds are U.

Evidence: `spectrum:B03`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-SPECTRUM-003 — analysis channel

**D12.** Channel selects analysis of left, right or both. The channel-combination algorithm, stereo summation/normalization and cancellation behavior of Both are U. This setting is not documented as changing audio output.

Evidence: `spectrum:B04, B02`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-SPECTRUM-004 — Refresh

**D12.** Refresh controls how often analysis occurs. Faster response trades greater CPU use for accuracy in the manual’s description. Exact domain, units, scheduling, update quantization, hidden-view behavior and wall-clock versus transport coupling are U.

Evidence: `spectrum:B05`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-SPECTRUM-005 — Avg

**D12.** Avg selects how many sample blocks are averaged for each display update. At one, each block is shown; larger values smooth the display over time. The domain, accumulation method, reset/priming, decibel-versus-linear averaging and weighting/window are U.

Evidence: `spectrum:B06`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-SPECTRUM-006 — Graph

**D12.** Graph switches between a single interpolated line and discrete frequency bins. Interpolation, bin positions, pixel rendering and amplitude calibration are U.

Evidence: `spectrum:B07`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-SPECTRUM-007 — maximum trace and reset

**D12.** Peak levels are retained until the song restarts. Max toggles display of accumulated maximum amplitude; when Max is enabled, clicking the display resets the maximum. Whether Max off clears accumulation, reset scope, restart event definition and reset timing are U.

Evidence: `spectrum:B02, B08`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-SPECTRUM-008 — horizontal scaling

**D12.** Scale X offers linear, logarithmic and semitone. Logarithmic and semitone use the same scaling, with top legends in Hz or note names respectively. Exact axis domain, note tuning reference, legend rounding and sample-rate-dependent limits are U.

Evidence: `spectrum:B09`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-SPECTRUM-009 — pointer readout

**D12.** Hovering the display shows a box with amplitude, frequency and note name at pointer location. This is a location readout, not a documented peak-picking or pitch-detector result. Units/rounding, off-graph behavior and frequency-to-note tie rules are U.

Evidence: `spectrum:B10`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-SPECTRUM-010 — manual range navigation

**D12.** Range/Auto selects manual or automatic dynamic range. In Range mode, amplitude-legending drags scroll vertically and zoom horizontally; Range sliders set minimum/maximum amplitude shown. Slider domain, allowed ordering, zoom limits and gestures outside the legending are U.

Evidence: `spectrum:B10`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-SPECTRUM-011 — Auto range

**D12.** Auto scales the display to incoming level; Range sliders and zooming are disabled. Algorithm, margins, hysteresis, decay and retained manual range are U.

Evidence: `spectrum:B10`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-SPECTRUM-012 — display location

**D12.** The title-bar button or double-click in the display toggles graph placement between device chain and Live’s main window. Geometry, focus/selection, keyboard accessibility and view/preset retention are U.

Evidence: `spectrum:B11`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-SPECTRUM-013 — target stored analysis state

**Dpkg.** Latest schema and eleven shipped Spectrum presets contain range/axis, analysis, Length, Window, channel, averaging and refresh fields. Window=3 is an observed stored code in these presets, not a named window function, selectable UI control, FFT kernel or mathematical law. Preset labels do not prove block counts or enum meanings.

Evidence: `PKG-SCHEMA:SpectrumAnalyzer; package-values.json device=Spectrum`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

### REQ-DEVICE-SPECTRUM-014 — numerical and lifecycle gaps

**U.** Exact 12.4.3 applicability of every D12 clause is U. FFT/window/kernel, dB normalization/floor, sample rates, latency, displayed numerical tolerances, silence/nonfinite handling, persistence, automation availability, undo/redo, cancellation, malformed state, engine/device failure and teardown have no target outcomes here.

Evidence: `No outcome evidence`; [source locators](#analysis-only-evidence).

## Evidence discipline and interactions

[Track mixer values](mixer-values.md) and [mix graph](mix-graph.md) are canonical
for their track/engine scopes. No traced caller path connects their fader curves,
silence floor, pan matrix or ramps to Utility's StereoGain control in this packet.
Reusing their mathematics would therefore invent device signal behavior. The
three new contracts explicitly leave gain/pan/mono normalization, filter response,
control ordering and smoothing unknown.

For Tuner, the manual supplies orientation and readout meaning. It does not give
pitch estimator, note-boundary ties, frequency/amplitude validity range, silence
state, confidence, cent/color thresholds, Hz rounding or acquisition latency.
The target's IgnoreTuningSystem field creates a concrete unresolved interaction
with Set tuning; its name alone supplies no semantics.

For Spectrum, Block/Avg/Refresh descriptions do not prove an FFT implementation,
window family, overlap, zero padding, amplitude normalization, effective latency
or averaging in linear magnitude versus power versus dB. Both-channel combination
and peak-history persistence/reset event details remain unknown. Window=3 is
specifically not a recovered window law.

The [device/rack draft](../specs/device-racks.md) owns generic host actions;
[Set structure](../specs/live-set-structure.md) owns its narrower T1 structure.
Neither makes these devices part of its released device subset. Save/reopen,
malformed state, undo/redo, cancellation, transport, automation, source/device
failure and teardown receive finite U cases in each device packet. Platform
accessibility/permissions remain cross-feature gaps; no figure inspection, binary
search or broad native analysis was performed solely to expand documentation.
